proposition: Letter 27 (ca. 830/1427, Herat?) records that Fīrūzshāh gave attention to Ibn Turka's case and that some of his confiscated property was (or, on MK's alternative reading, was to be) restored; Ibn Turka asks him to pursue the case and restore the stipend, saying friends had freed him from imprisonment by the dīvān's debt- and tax-collectors.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to Amīr Fīrūzshāh
mediation.where: Munshaʾāt-i Turka letter 27; MS Majlis 10196 f. 160a
mediation.note: Written by a supplicant asking a ruler or official for clemency, relief or a stipend; framed to win the favour asked, not as a neutral report.

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, summarising, dating and identifying the letter(s)
mediation.note: MK's footnote: he may be requesting the restoration rather than acknowledging it
